author: hker
storyTitle: Hong Kong’s security law is going to devastate its economy
text:
TL;DR: limiting freedom of expression in name of national security, without a just trial.
Stretching a bit, we call it the freedom from fear (of unjust prosecution), which is the—arguably justified—distrust of the rule by law in China (not the rule of law that Hong Kong previously had). Note that Hong Kong people are using “Freedom from Fear” [1] differently from how US is using it [2].
Chinese courts work very differently from Hong Kong ones: they swing with politics. Many people have been—as perceived by Hong Kongers—unjustly detained or prosecuted (such as the milk powder incidents [3], the two Canadians in China after the Huawei case [4], or the more recent whistleblower Li Wenliang). And those people, in some cases, are sued for charges such as spying or subversion, which is the main theme of the national security law.
Given that Chinese agents extracted Hong Kongers in the Causeway Bay Books disappearances [5], Hong Kongers fear that the new national security law (which allows state agents to police Hong Kong [6]) means that Hong Kongers (and perhaps foreigners) may face state agents extraction from Hong Kong. To many Hong Kongers, voicing out for social injustice could mean instability in China, and could mean theft of state secret or subversion as CCP see it.
Hence it is limiting freedom of speech.
[1]: “Freedom from Fear” is a slogan in Hong Kong protests, see for example this image https://cdn.cnn.com/cnnnext/dam/assets/181114165731-hong-kon...

storyTitle: The Value of Downvoting, Or, How Hacker News Gets It Wrong (2009)
text:
> the most notable difference between Hacker News and Reddit is that it's impossible to downvote anything on Hacker News. [..] It's an interesting design decision, but ultimately a bad one, in my opinion.
That's not true (as the author realized himself). And I don't agree with the author; letting people downvote is unfortunate in my opinion, and a bad design decision. The possibility to downvote encourages misuse. I don't see any reason for the majority of downvotes I come across; mostly it's just other opinions that don't suit a few people; often it's even the correct presentation of the facts that has been downvoted.
Most people on HN are anonymous. Downvoting is even more anonymous; there is usually no record from who the downvotes come. If you're interested in the effects of anonymity to people, watch this part of Zimbardo's very interesting lecture: https://youtu.be/OsFEV35tWsg?t=959. The anonymity of the web, or the masses, gives these people a power that obviously overwhelms them. There were experiments which demonstrated how it can play out when ordinary people suddenly gain power (see e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_prison_experiment).
The possibility to downvote promotes the bad in people. And it is not even necessary. If you like a comment or story for whatever reason, you can upvote. That's already enough to promote popular content, and demote unpopular content. And if a comment violates site rules, it can be flagged. Of course also flagging can be misused (as it is very popular e.g. on Lobsters); this can be mitigated in that the admin kicks out people who misuse flagging. And that's likely the issue: the admin prefers delegating work to the community, which is likely the main and only reason why the downvoting features persists.

My cousin was a car dealer, and, while I love her to pieces, when she started talking about her job and their attitudes towards customers ("Buyers are liars"), I absolutely understood how just filling a role can change how you fundamentally behave (see: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_prison_experiment for more details)
Your last scenario, btw - is actually the exact way to buy a vehicle from these jerks.  Do the research, find the absolute best price, end of month/quarter/year dealer incentives included, and then find a dealer that's rated well for service - and give them a Yes/No offer, all in (including shipping, transfer, paperwork, whatever the hell they want to make up - you don't care, just as long as the bottom line is less than your number) - and a time limit.
